fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but Micah says it the other way around. He tells the leaders, "You hate good and love evil." (Micah 3:2). These are the rulers he just asked, "Should you not know justice?" The text says hate for good and love for evil.

The text says something different. Micah says they will cry out to the LORD, "…but He will not answer them." (Micah 3:4). I wish I had a happier answer to hand you on this one, friend. Micah describes a time when the cry goes up and no answer comes.

The LORD says these prophets "…declare war against one who puts nothing in their mouths…" (Micah 3:5). They proclaim peace while they chew, and the war goes to the one who gives them nothing. I've been in kitchens with more honest signals than that.

The verse gives the reason itself. The seers and diviners "…will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God." (Micah 3:7). A seer with nothing to see has nothing left to say. You know when everybody in the meeting turns to you for the answer and you've got NOTHING? That's the hand over the mouth.

The text doesn't say that. It says they "…will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God." (Micah 3:7). Nobody shushes them in this verse, friend. The quiet comes because God gives no answer.

Micah says, "…I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage…" (Micah 3:8). That's the 'however' after all the silence in the verses before. The seers will have no answer from God, and Micah has the Spirit of the LORD. His power comes from there, not from his own muscles, which in my case would be a relief.

The king's court never comes up in this verse. Micah says, "…I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage…" (Micah 3:8). No royal backing, no palace connections. Just the Spirit of the LORD, filling him with justice and courage.
Micah says they are the ones "…who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity." (Micah 3:10). The building materials are the problem. That's a shaky foundation, friend.

Prayer and praise aren't in this verse. Micah says they "…build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity." (Micah 3:10). Those are hard words to hand the leaders of a city, friend. Micah doesn't soften them one bit.
Yes, Micah says, "…her priests teach for a price…" (Micah 3:11). Teaching, with a price tag stuck right on it. It's there in his list with the leaders and the prophets. He names all three.

They say, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster can come upon us." (Micah 3:11). Notice that Micah says they lean upon the LORD even as they judge for a bribe and teach for a price. Bribes and all, and they STILL say no disaster can come. Micah's very next words say otherwise.

They don't say that. Micah says they lean upon the LORD, saying, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster can come upon us." (Micah 3:11). I think they sound confident, not worried. They say He is among them.

Micah says, "Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field…" (Micah 3:12). He pictures Zion plowed like a field. I think that's a hard picture to take in. Micah says it's because of them.
